mainTopic: Partial corpse-טומאות, the 'can it be touched' rule for sealed bones and eggs, and which mice count as a טמא שרץ
overview: The amud opens with three things from a dead body that are טמא: a full ladle of רקב, a bone the size of a barley grain, and the גולל and דופק. Each of these spreads טומאה in only two of the three usual ways (מגע, משא, אהל), and each one is missing a different way. Next the גמרא turns to the thigh bone of a נבלה or שרץ. A ברייתא teaches that a sealed bone does not make you טמא by touch, but a pierced one does, because the rule is that what can be touched is טמא. רבי זירא and רב פפא challenge this rule with an animal in its skin and a kidney in its fat. Both are answered: neither is really sealed. רב אושעיא then rules that a bone someone only planned to pierce already counts as open. A new משנה teaches about a שרץ egg and a mouse that is half flesh and half earth. The גמרא brings פסוקים for these rules, gives two versions of רבי יהושע בן לוי's condition on the mouse, and starts a ברייתא showing that a sea mouse is not טמא. That ברייתא continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Three corpse-impurities that each have only two of the three ways
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא opens by saying there are three טומאות from a מת. Each one has two ways of spreading טומאה but not the third. It names them: a ladle of רקב, a barley-sized bone, and the גולל and דופק.
steps.simpleTranslation: There are three kinds of טומאה that come from a dead body. Each one makes things טמא in two ways, but not in the third way. They are: a full ladle of corpse-dust, a bone the size of a barley grain, and a grave cover with its side-wall.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא states a general rule and lists its three items. This line sets up the three detailed clauses that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are three ways טומאת מת spreads: מגע (touching), משא (carrying), and אהל (sharing a roof). Each item here has a 'partial' status. It is still טומאת מת, but it works in only two of those three ways. The next steps say which way each one is missing.

keyTerms.meaning: Impurities that 'separate' from, or come out of, a dead body (not the whole body itself)
Two (ways of making טמא) are in each one
Rotted remains of a dead body that have turned into dust
A ladle; a full ladle is the set amount for רקב
A piece of bone as big as a barley grain
The cover-stone of a grave (גולל) and the side-wall it rests on (דופק)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think these items are not real טומאת מת. They are fully טומאת מת. They just spread their טומאה in only two of the three usual ways.

phrases.english: Three impurities come out from a corpse,
two (ways of making impure) are in each one,
phrases.notes: The three 'ways' are touching, carrying, and being under one roof with it.

phrases.english: and the third is not in them,
and these are they: a full ladle of corpse-dust,
and a bone the size of a barley grain,
and a grave cover and grave side-wall.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the ברייתא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Three corpse-derived טומאות each spread טומאה in two of the three ways, but not the third.

steps.title: A ladle of corpse-dust: carrying and tent, but not touching
steps.stepSummary: A full ladle of רקב makes things טמא through משא and אהל, but not through מגע. Touching is found in one of the other items.
steps.simpleTranslation: A full ladle of corpse-dust makes things impure if you carry it or are under one roof with it, but not if you touch it. So where do we find touching? In one of the other two items.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא explains the first item, the ladle of רקב. It tells us which way is missing (touching), and then points out that touching shows up in one of the other two items.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רקב works by משא and אהל but has no מגע. The question 'where is its touching?' is not a challenge. It is a way of showing the pattern: the way that is missing here is found in one of the other items on the list.

keyTerms.meaning: Carrying; becoming טמא by lifting or moving the source of טומאה
Touching; becoming טמא by direct contact
'Where is its touching?' This asks where the missing way is found
With one of them, meaning one of the other items on the list

phrases.english: A full ladle of corpse-dust:
it makes impure by carrying and by tent,
phrases.notes: 'Tent' here means being under the same roof as the טומאה.

phrases.english: but it does not make impure by touching.
And where is its touching?
With one of them.
phrases.notes: Touching is found in one of the other two items, the bone or the grave cover.

steps.triggerLanguage: מְלֹא תַרְוָוד רָקָב מְטַמֵּא בְּמַשָּׂא וּבְאֹהֶל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the first item from the list in step 1
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A full ladle of רקב makes things טמא by משא and אהל, but not by מגע.

steps.title: A barley-sized bone: carrying and touching, but not tent
steps.stepSummary: An עצם כשעורה makes things טמא through משא and מגע, but not through אהל. The tent-way is found in one of the other items.
steps.simpleTranslation: A bone the size of a barley grain makes things impure if you carry it or touch it, but not if you are only under one roof with it. So where do we find the tent-way? In one of the other two items.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא explains the second item, the small bone. Its missing way is אהל, and that way is found in one of the other items.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the missing way is different. The bone has מגע and משא, but no אהל. This shows that each item on the list lacks a different way.

keyTerms.meaning: Tent or roof; becoming טמא by being under one roof with the טומאה
Its tent-impurity
Makes something or someone טמא

phrases.english: A bone the size of a barley grain:
it makes impure by carrying and by touching,
but it does not make impure by tent.
And where is its tent-impurity?
With one of them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the second item from the list in step 1, following the same pattern as step 2
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A barley-sized bone makes things טמא by משא and מגע, but not by אהל.

steps.title: Grave cover and side-wall: touching and tent, but not carrying
steps.stepSummary: The גולל and דופק make things טמא through מגע and אהל, but not through משא. Carrying is found in one of the other items. This finishes the three-part pattern.
steps.simpleTranslation: The grave cover and side-wall make things impure if you touch them or are under one roof with them, but not if you carry them. So where do we find carrying? In one of the other two items.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא explains the third and last item. Its missing way is משא. Now the full list is done.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With this item, each of the three ways has been missing exactly once. רקב has no מגע, the bone has no אהל, and the גולל ודופק have no משא. Each missing way shows up in the other two items, so the three items fit together like puzzle pieces.

keyTerms.meaning: Its carrying-impurity
Does not make טמא (in that particular way)
The טומאה that comes from a dead body

steps.whatToRemember: Here is a simple chart. רקב = משא + אהל (no מגע). עצם כשעורה = משא + מגע (no אהל). גולל ודופק = מגע + אהל (no משא). Each one is missing a different way.

phrases.english: The grave cover and side-wall:
they make impure by touching and by tent,
but they do not make impure by carrying.
And where is its carrying-impurity?
With one of them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the third item and finishes the pattern begun in steps 2 and 3
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Each of the three items is missing a different one of the three ways of spreading טומאה, and each missing way is found in the other two items.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The גולל and דופק make things טמא by מגע and אהל, but not by משא.

steps.title: A sealed thigh bone does not pass on טומאה by touch
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about the thigh bone of a נבלה or שרץ and brings a ברייתא: the פסוק says 'its נבלה', not a sealed thigh bone.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה spoke about the thigh bone of a נבלה and of a שרץ. The רבנן taught: the פסוק says 'its carcass', and that does not include a sealed thigh bone.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה and brings a ברייתא that gives the source for it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The marrow inside the bone counts as נבלה, but the bone itself does not. Since the bone is closed, touching it is not touching the נבלה, so the person stays טהור. The ברייתא reads this from the word 'בנבלתה'.

keyTerms.meaning: A thigh bone, the long bone that holds marrow
An animal that died without proper שחיטה
One of the small creeping creatures that pass on טומאה
Sealed, closed up with no opening

phrases.english: The thigh bone of a carcass and the thigh bone of a creeping creature, etc.
The Rabbis taught:
"Its carcass": but not a sealed thigh bone.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה; it does not build on the three טומאות of a מת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Touching a sealed thigh bone of a נבלה or שרץ does not make a person טמא, learned from 'בנבלתה'.

steps.title: What if the bone was pierced?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא raises a possible thought: maybe even a bone with a hole stays טהור.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think that even if the bone was pierced, touching it still does not make you טמא.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא sets up a possible mistake so it can correct it in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 excluded a thigh bone from the word 'בנבלתה'. Someone could think every thigh bone is excluded, even an open one. The ברייתא asks whether the hole changes anything.

keyTerms.meaning: 'You might think', a ברייתא's way of raising a thought it will reject
Even
It was pierced, it has a hole in it

phrases.english: One might think: even if it was pierced?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests how far the rule from step 5 goes.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does a pierced thigh bone also stay טהור to the touch, like a sealed one?

steps.title: If you can reach it, it makes you טמא
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק 'הנוגע… יטמא' teaches the rule: if the טומאה can be touched, it makes you טמא; if not, you stay טהור.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'one who touches… will be טמא'. Something that can be touched is טמא, and something that cannot be touched is טהור.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers step 6: a pierced bone does make you טמא, because now the marrow can be reached.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key is not 'bone or not bone' but whether touching is possible. A sealed bone blocks the marrow, so you stay טהור. A pierced bone lets you reach the marrow, so it is like touching the נבלה itself.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The פסוק teaches', bringing a verse to settle the question
The one who touches
It is possible to touch
Ritually impure / ritually pure

steps.whatToRemember: The rule: if the טומאה can be reached by touch, it makes you טמא. If it is fully closed off, you stay טהור.

phrases.english: The verse teaches: "One who touches … will be impure,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 11:39. The dots mean part of the פסוק is skipped: 'its carcass'.

phrases.english: what is possible to touch is impure,
and what is impossible to touch is pure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A pierced bone does make you טמא; the test is whether the טומאה can be touched.
steps.whyThisMatters: This 'can it be touched' rule is what the next two challenges attack.

steps.title: Then an animal in its skin should not make you טמא
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא asks אביי: by this rule, a dead animal still in its skin is covered, so touching it should not make you טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said to אביי: If so, an animal in its skin should not make you טמא!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא challenges the rule from step 7 with a common case that seems to break it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The skin covers the flesh the way the bone covers the marrow. So by the rule, touching a whole נבלה should only be touching the skin. But everyone knows touching a נבלה makes you טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: 'But if so', used to show a rule leads to a strange result
In its skin, with its hide still on
It will make something טמא

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said to Abaye:
But if so,
an animal in its skin should not make impure?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מֵעַתָּה, בְּהֵמָה בְּעוֹרָהּ לֹא תְּטַמֵּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the rule taught in step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that something that cannot be touched does not make you טמא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The skin covers the flesh like a sealed bone covers the marrow, so a whole נבלה should never make you טמא by touch, which cannot be right.

steps.title: An animal has many openings
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers: look how many openings an animal has; through them the flesh can be reached.
steps.simpleTranslation: Go out and see how many openings it has!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers רבי זירא and shows the animal in its skin really fits the rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The skin is not a full seal like a closed bone. An animal has openings like the mouth and nose, so its flesh can be touched. That makes it 'possible to touch', so it makes you טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Go out and see', look at the real world
Holes, openings

phrases.english: Go out and see
phrases.notes: אביי is the one answering here, even though the גמרא doesn't name him.

phrases.english: how many openings it has!

steps.triggerLanguage: פּוֹק חֲזִי כַּמָּה נְקָבִים יֵשׁ בָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Factual distinction: the case is not really sealed.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: An animal in its skin is fully covered, like a sealed bone.
steps.terutzMaskana: An animal has many openings, so its flesh can be touched and it makes you טמא.

steps.title: Then a kidney in its fat should not make you טמא
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא asks רבא: a kidney fully wrapped in its fat is covered, so by the rule it should not make you טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said to רבא: If so, a kidney inside its fat should not make you טמא!
steps.whatsHappening: A second challenge to the same rule, this time from a kidney covered in fat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The kidney of a נבלה sits wrapped in fat, so touching it seems to be touching only the fat around it. By the rule from step 7, it should not make you טמא. This case has no mouth or nose, so the answer from step 9 does not help.

keyTerms.meaning: Kidney
Its fat, the fat around the kidney

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said to Rava:
But if so,
a kidney in its fat should not make impure?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מֵעַתָּה, כּוּלְיָא בְּחֶלְבָּהּ לֹא תְּטַמֵּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel challenge to the same rule, like step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that something that cannot be touched does not make you טמא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A kidney wrapped in fat seems completely covered, so by the rule it should not make you טמא by touch.

steps.title: Strands stick out from the kidney
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers: look how many strands come out of the kidney; those can be touched.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and see how many strands come out from it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers רב פפא and shows the kidney is not fully sealed either.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Strands come out of the kidney through the fat. Since a person can touch those strands, the kidney is 'possible to touch'. So the rule from step 7 stands.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Come and see'
Strands, thin threads of tissue
Stretch out, come out

steps.whatToRemember: Both challenges fail for the same reason: the animal and the kidney are not fully sealed, so the rule from step 7 stays in place.

phrases.english: Come and see
phrases.notes: רבא is the one answering here.

phrases.english: how many strands come out from it.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא חֲזִי כַּמָּה חוּטִין נִמְשָׁכִין הֵימֶנָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 10, the same way step 9 answered step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Factual distinction: the case is not really sealed.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A kidney in its fat is fully covered.
steps.terutzMaskana: Strands come out of the kidney, so it can be touched and it makes you טמא.

steps.title: A bone someone planned to make a hole in
steps.stepSummary: רב אושעיא asks about a thigh bone that someone planned to make a hole in but never did. Is it treated as sealed or as already open?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אושעיא asked: if a person planned to make a hole in the thigh bone but did not do it yet, what is the law? Is a bone that only lacks a hole treated like something still missing a real action (so it stays like a sealed bone)? Or not?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אושעיא asks a new question about the sealed thigh bone from the earlier משנה. What if someone planned to make a hole in it but never did?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier משנה taught two rules. A sealed bone does not make you טמא by touch. A bone with a hole does. The question is whether a person's plan to make a hole is enough, or whether the missing hole is a real missing step that keeps the bone in the 'sealed' group.

keyTerms.meaning: He planned or intended (in his mind)
Making a hole
Still missing an action; something must still be done before the law applies
A thigh bone

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not about what you physically touch. It is about whether a plan alone changes the bone's status even though it is still sealed.

phrases.english: Rav Oshaya asked:
If one planned to make a hole in it
phrases.notes: 'It' is the sealed thigh bone from the earlier משנה.

phrases.english: but did not make the hole, what is the law?
Is 'lacking a hole' like 'lacking an action',
or not?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new question about the sealed thigh bone, moving away from the animal and kidney questions.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does a plan to make a hole in a sealed thigh bone make it count as open, or does the missing hole keep it sealed?

steps.title: רב אושעיא answers his own question
steps.stepSummary: רב אושעיא decides that a missing hole is not a missing action, so the plan alone is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then he answered it himself: a bone that only lacks a hole is not treated like something still missing an action.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אושעיא answers his own question. The bone is not stuck in the 'sealed' group, so once he plans to make the hole, it counts as open.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Making the hole is not seen as a real missing step that holds up the law. So the person's plan already gives the bone the status of an open bone, even though no hole was made yet.

keyTerms.meaning: He then resolved it himself
Is like, is treated as

steps.whatToRemember: רב אושעיא rules that a missing hole is not a missing action. Once a person plans to make a hole in the thigh bone, it already counts as open.

phrases.english: He then resolved it:
lacking a hole
is not like lacking an action.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question asked in step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A missing hole is not a missing action, so the plan alone gives the bone the status of an open bone.

steps.title: The egg of a שרץ: sealed versus with a hole
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that a sealed שרץ egg with a developing creature inside does not make you טמא by touch, but once it has any hole, it does.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: the egg of a שרץ in which the young creature has started to form is טהור. If it has a hole of any size, it is טמא.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It rules on the egg of a שרץ, sealed versus with a hole.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This uses the same rule from step 7: טומאה you cannot touch does not make you טמא. While the egg is closed, the creature inside cannot be touched. Even the smallest hole makes it reachable, so touching the egg now makes you טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for מַתְנִיתִין, 'our משנה'
One of the small creeping creatures whose dead body is a source of טומאה
Formed; the young creature's body has started to take shape inside
Any amount at all, even the smallest

phrases.english: MISHNA: The egg of a creeping creature
in which the young has formed is pure,
phrases.notes: Literally 'embroidered.' The young creature's body has started to take shape inside the egg.

phrases.english: if it has a hole of any size, it is impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה that uses the same 'can it be touched?' rule on a new case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A sealed שרץ egg with a formed young creature inside does not make you טמא by touch. Once it has any hole, it does.

steps.title: A mouse that is half flesh and half earth
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that for a mouse that is half flesh and half earth, touching the flesh makes you טמא and touching the earth does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: A mouse that is half flesh and half earth: one who touches the flesh is טמא; one who touches the earth is טהור.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a second case: a mouse that is half flesh and half earth. Only the flesh part makes you טמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only the part that is truly a creature's flesh counts as a שרץ. The earth part is just earth, so touching it does nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: A mouse, one of the שרצים
Earth, soil
The one who touches

phrases.english: A mouse that is half flesh and half earth,
phrases.notes: This is a mouse that grows out of the ground and is only partly formed.

phrases.english: one who touches the flesh is impure,
one who touches the earth is pure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second case in the same משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only the flesh part of the half-formed mouse makes you טמא. The earth part does not.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: the earth right against the flesh
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה adds that even touching the earth part that lies right against the flesh makes you טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: even one who touches the earth that is right next to the flesh is טמא.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה disagrees in part with the first opinion in the משנה. He makes the טומאה area a little bigger.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion draws a sharp line between flesh and earth. רבי יהודה holds that the earth directly against the flesh is also טמא. The rest of the earth stays טהור even according to him.

keyTerms.meaning: Even, also; adds to the earlier ruling
That is right opposite, or right against

steps.whatToRemember: In the half-formed mouse, all agree that the flesh is טמא. רבי יהודה adds the earth right against the flesh.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אַף הַנּוֹגֵעַ בָּאֲדָמָה
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: even one who touches the earth
that is right against the flesh is impure.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אַף הַנּוֹגֵעַ בָּאֲדָמָה שֶׁכְּנֶגֶד הַבָּשָׂר טָמֵא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the first opinion in step 15 and widens the area that is טמא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The earth right against the mouse's flesh is also טמא.

steps.title: A פסוק source for the egg and thigh bone of a שרץ
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from the word 'הטמאים' that a שרץ egg and a שרץ thigh bone can also carry טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: the רבנן taught: 'the impure ones' comes to include the egg of a שרץ and the thigh bone of a שרץ.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and brings a ברייתא that gives a source from the פסוק. It shows that the egg and the thigh bone of a שרץ are sources of טומאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said a שרץ egg with a hole makes you טמא, but where do we learn that an egg can carry טומאה at all? The extra word 'הטמאים' in ויקרא 11:31 adds the egg and the thigh bone to the list of things that make a person טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains the משנה
'The impure ones', a word in the פסוק about שרצים
To include; the word adds more cases

phrases.english: GEMARA: The Rabbis taught:
"The impure ones"
comes to include the egg of a creeping creature
and the thigh bone of a creeping creature.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הַטְּמֵאִים לְרַבּוֹת בֵּיצַת הַשֶּׁרֶץ וְקוּלִית הַשֶּׁרֶץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the פסוק source behind the משנה's ruling on the שרץ egg in step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The word 'הטמאים' includes a שרץ egg and a שרץ thigh bone as sources of טומאה.

steps.title: The egg must have a developing creature inside
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא learns from the word 'השרץ' that a שרץ egg is only טמא once a creature has started forming inside it.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think an egg is טמא even if nothing has formed inside. So the פסוק says 'השרץ.' Just as a שרץ is a formed creature, the egg too must have a creature forming inside.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא from step 17 continues and adds a limit: not every שרץ egg is טמא, only one with a developing creature inside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 17 said a שרץ egg can carry טומאה. Now the ברייתא narrows that rule. The word 'השרץ' links the egg to a real creature, so a plain egg with nothing formed inside does not count.

keyTerms.meaning: Tissue formed; a creature has started developing inside
'One might think...' This opens a wrong assumption that the ברייתא is about to reject
'The פסוק teaches...' This brings the verse that settles the question
The egg of a שרץ

phrases.english: One might think: even if tissue has not developed in it?
The verse teaches: 'The creeping animal'
Just as a שרץ has developed tissue,
so too, only a שרץ egg in which tissue has developed.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל אֲפִילּוּ לֹא רִיקְּמָה? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the ברייתא's ruling from step 17 that a שרץ egg can carry טומאה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A שרץ egg is טמא only if a creature has begun forming inside it.

steps.title: The egg or bone must have a hole you can touch through
steps.stepSummary: From 'הנוגע... יטמא' the ברייתא learns that you only become טמא if you can actually touch the inside.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think it is טמא even without a hole. So the פסוק says 'Whoever touches... becomes טמא.' If you can touch it, it is טמא. If you cannot touch it, it is טהור.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds a second condition: the egg (or thigh bone) must be open with a hole, so you can really touch what is inside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even a developing egg is sealed by its shell. The פסוק speaks about 'touching,' so if the inside cannot be reached, there is no touching and no טומאה. This is the source for the משנה's rule in step 14.

keyTerms.meaning: They were pierced, they have a hole
It is possible to touch
Pure, not טמא

phrases.english: One might think: even if they were not pierced?
phrases.notes: 'They' means the egg and the thigh bone from step 17.

phrases.english: The verse teaches: 'Whoever touches... shall be טמא,'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 11:31. The dots mean the ברייתא skips the middle words of the פסוק.

phrases.english: something it is possible to touch is טמא,
and something it is impossible to touch is טהור.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל אֲפִילּוּ לֹא נִיקְּבוּ? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second condition after the developing-creature condition of step 18
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A שרץ egg or thigh bone is טמא only when it has a hole, so the inside can be touched.

steps.title: How big must the hole be?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks what size hole is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how big must its hole be?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks a follow-up question and sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 19 said a hole is needed. Now the ברייתא wants the smallest size that counts.

keyTerms.meaning: A hole, a piercing

phrases.english: And how big is its hole?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the size of the hole required in step 19
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The smallest hole size that makes the egg or bone touchable

steps.title: A hole as thin as a hair is enough
steps.stepSummary: Even a hair-width hole counts, because your own attached hair reaching inside counts as your touch.
steps.simpleTranslation: As wide as a strand of hair, because it is possible to touch the inside with a strand of hair.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers: a tiny hole the width of a hair is enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The test from step 19 is whether touching is possible. A hair still attached to a person's head or beard counts as part of the person's body. Putting that attached hair through the hole can therefore count as touching the impurity inside. Even a hair-width hole is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: Like a strand of hair, the thinnest measure

steps.whatToRemember: A שרץ egg makes you טמא only if (1) a creature has started forming inside, and (2) it has a hole, even one as thin as a hair.

phrases.english: Like a strand of hair,
since it is possible to touch with a strand of hair.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 20
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A hole the width of a hair is enough, since touching the inside with your own attached hair counts as touching.

steps.title: The mouse's flesh must run its whole length
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי says the half-flesh mouse makes you טמא only if the flesh has formed along its entire length.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: a mouse that is half flesh, etc. רבי יהושע בן לוי said: this is only when the flesh has developed along its whole length.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה's mouse from step 15, and רבי יהושע בן לוי adds a condition to that ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said touching the flesh part makes you טמא. רבי יהושע בן לוי limits this: the flesh must stretch along the whole mouse, from head to foot. If only part of its length is flesh, touching it does not make you טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: A mouse that is half flesh and half earth
Developed, formed into a creature
Along its entire length

phrases.english: 'A mouse that is half...' etc.
phrases.notes: The גמרא quotes just the start of the משנה from step 15; 'etc.' means the rest of that line.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
This is only when it developed along its entire length.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַכְבָּר שֶׁחֶצְיוֹ וְכוּ׳ אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the egg topic and returns to the mouse ruling of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Touching the flesh of the half-earth mouse makes you טמא only if the flesh formed along its whole length.

steps.title: Another version: the condition is said about רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: Some place רבי יהושע בן לוי's condition on רבי יהודה's ruling about the earth next to the flesh.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some teach this on the end of the משנה: רבי יהודה says, even someone who touches the earth next to the flesh is טמא. רבי יהושע בן לוי said: this is only when it developed along its entire length.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of where רבי יהושע בן לוי's condition belongs: on רבי יהודה's ruling from step 16.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version, the whole-length condition limits the משנה's basic rule about touching the flesh. In this version, it only limits רבי יהודה's extra rule, that touching the earth beside the flesh also makes you טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: Some teach it (place this statement) differently
The later part of a משנה
Right next to the flesh

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יהושע בן לוי's words are the same in both versions. Only the part of the משנה they attach to has changed.

phrases.english: Some teach it on the latter clause:
Rabbi Yehuda says:

phrases.aramaic: אַף הַנּוֹגֵעַ בָּאֲדָמָה שֶׁכְּנֶגֶד בָּשָׂר טָמֵא,
phrases.english: Even one who touches the earth next to the flesh is טמא.
Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
This is only when it developed along its entire length.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second version of where step 22's condition belongs
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In this version, רבי יהודה's rule (touching earth beside the flesh makes you טמא) applies only when the flesh formed along the mouse's whole length.

steps.title: The practical difference between the two versions
steps.stepSummary: If the condition is taught on the first clause, it applies even more to the last clause. If it is taught only on the last clause, then the first clause needs no full development of flesh.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whoever places רבי יהושע בן לוי's condition on the first clause would apply it even more to the last clause. Whoever places it on the last clause holds that in the first clause the mouse makes you טמא even if the flesh has not formed along its whole length.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what difference it makes whether רבי יהושע בן לוי's condition is attached to the first clause of the משנה or to the last clause.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first clause (the תנא קמא) is about touching the flesh part itself. The last clause (רבי יהודה) is about touching the earth next to the flesh, which is a weaker case. If you need full flesh even to become טמא by touching the flesh, then for touching the earth you certainly need it. But if the condition was only said about the earth case, then touching the flesh makes you טמא with no such requirement.

keyTerms.meaning: The first clause of a משנה or ברייתא
The last clause of a משנה or ברייתא
All the more so
Fully developed; here, the flesh formed along the whole length of the mouse

steps.whatToRemember: Version 1 puts the condition on both clauses. Version 2 puts it only on רבי יהודה's 'earth next to the flesh' case.

phrases.english: The one who teaches it on the first clause
phrases.notes: 'It' is רבי יהושע בן לוי's condition from step 22, that the flesh must be formed along the whole length.

phrases.english: all the more so on the latter clause
and the one who teaches it on the latter clause
but the first clause
even though it has not fully developed

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן דְּמַתְנֵי לַהּ אַרֵישָׁא כׇּל שֶׁכֵּן אַסֵּיפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the practical result of the two versions given in Steps 22 and 23.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Version 1: the full-flesh condition applies to both clauses. Version 2: it applies only to רבי יהודה's case; in the first clause, touching the flesh makes you טמא even without full development.

steps.title: Maybe a sea mouse is also included
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא suggests that since the פסוק just says 'mouse,' even a sea creature called 'mouse' might be טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: since the פסוק says 'mouse,' I would think that even a sea mouse is included, because it is also called 'mouse.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new ברייתא opens a new topic. It raises a first idea: the word עכבר might include anything named 'mouse,' even a sea creature.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the starting assumption, based only on the name. The ברייתא will now test it with logic and then settle it with a פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: Mouse; one of the eight שרצים that make a person טמא
A 'sea mouse,' a sea creature that has the name 'mouse'
I would understand; introduces a first, possible reading

phrases.english: The Sages taught: since it says 'mouse'
I would understand even a sea mouse
since its name is 'mouse'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new ברייתא about which creatures count as עכבר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: First idea: the name 'mouse' alone might include a sea mouse.

steps.title: Logic says only a land mouse, like the weasel
steps.stepSummary: The weasel next to it in the פסוק is a land animal, so the mouse should also mean a land animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: But logic says otherwise: the תורה made the weasel טמא and the mouse טמא. Just as the weasel is a land animal, so the mouse is a land animal.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא offers a logical argument against including the sea mouse, by comparing the mouse to the weasel listed next to it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The comparison focuses on what kind of creature the weasel is: one that grows on land. If the mouse is like the weasel, then only a land mouse counts, and the sea mouse is out.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a logical argument; logic would tell us
Weasel; listed next to the mouse in the פסוק
A species that grows on land

phrases.english: But it is logical
He made the weasel טמא and made the mouse טמא

phrases.aramaic: מָה חוּלְדָּה מִין הַגָּדֵל עַל הָאָרֶץ
phrases.english: just as a weasel is a species that grows on land

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַכְבָּר מִין הַגָּדֵל עַל הָאָרֶץ
phrases.english: so too the mouse is a species that grows on land

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Argues against the first idea in Step 25.
steps.raayaObject: That only a land mouse is טמא
steps.raayaSupportSource: Comparing the mouse to the weasel, which is a land animal

steps.title: Or logic says anything named 'mouse,' like the weasel
steps.stepSummary: You could compare differently: just as anything named 'weasel' counts, anything named 'mouse' counts, even a sea mouse.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or go this way: the תורה made the weasel טמא and the mouse טמא. Just as the weasel means anything called 'weasel,' so the mouse means anything called 'mouse,' even a sea mouse, since it is called 'mouse.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא pushes back on the logic of Step 26 by making the same comparison in a different way that leads to the opposite answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both arguments compare the mouse to the weasel. Step 26 compared them by where they live; this step compares them by name. Since the comparison can go either way, logic alone cannot decide, so a פסוק is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: Go this way; introduces another way to run the same comparison

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new opinion that wins. It just shows that the weasel comparison can point either way, so logic alone does not settle the question.

phrases.english: Or go this way
He made the weasel טמא and made the mouse טמא
just as 'weasel' means anything named 'weasel'
so too 'mouse' means anything named 'mouse'
even a sea mouse, since its name is 'mouse'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 26 with an opposite comparison.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects relying on the logical comparison of Step 26
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The weasel comparison could just as well be based on the name, which would include the sea mouse

steps.title: The פסוק says 'on the land'
steps.stepSummary: The words 'על הארץ' in the פסוק show that only a land mouse is טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is why the פסוק says: 'on the land.'
steps.whatsHappening: Since logic could go either way, the ברייתא settles the question with the words 'על הארץ' from the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק describes these שרצים as creatures that swarm 'on the land.' This excludes the sea mouse, even though it has the same name.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק teaches; introduces the deciding words of a פסוק
On the land; from ויקרא 11:29

steps.whatToRemember: A sea mouse is not טמא, because the פסוק says 'על הארץ.'

phrases.english: The verse states: 'on the land'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles the standoff between Steps 26 and 27 using the פסוק.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Only a land mouse is טמא; the sea mouse is excluded by 'על הארץ.'

steps.title: Maybe 'on the land' depends on where the mouse is
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא worries that 'על הארץ' could be read as: any mouse is טמא while on land, and not טמא once it goes into the sea.
steps.simpleTranslation: If we learn only from 'on the land,' I might think that a mouse on land makes you טמא, but if it went down into the sea it does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא raises a problem with relying only on 'על הארץ': it might be misread as being about the mouse's location, not its species. This sets up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 28 used 'על הארץ' to mean 'a land species.' But the words could also mean 'while it is on land,' which would make טומאה depend on where the creature is right now. The ברייתא will need to rule out this reading.

keyTerms.meaning: One might think; introduces a possible wrong reading
It makes things טמא

phrases.english: If only 'on the land'
one might think: on the land, it makes טמא
if it went down to the sea, it does not make טמא

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי עַל הָאָרֶץ יָכוֹל עַל הָאָרֶץ יְטַמֵּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions whether the words in Step 28 are enough on their own.
steps.kashyaTarget: Relying only on 'על הארץ' to exclude the sea mouse
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'On the land' could describe where the mouse is right now rather than what kind of creature it is, which would make any mouse lose its טומאה in the sea.
